raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Adds an opt-in ASGI middleware that strips Unicode tag characters (U+E0020 to U+E007F) from request bodies sent to the LLM generation endpoints, enabled with `VLLM_ENABLE_UNICODE_FILTERING_MIDDLEWARE=true`. Supersedes #41762 (closed), which had an approval on the same design.

## Claims

- Tag characters are invisible to humans but are tokenized by the model and can steer or destabilize generations; with the flag set they are removed before the request reaches the handler, for both encodings a JSON client can use (raw UTF-8 and `\uDB40\uDCxx` escapes).
- Covers `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions/batch`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages` and `/cohere/v2/chat`; all other routes, methods and characters (including emoji) are untouched.
- Off by default; zero cost on clean payloads beyond two substring checks on the buffered body.
- Fixes a bug present in the earlier revisions of this PR: the replayed `receive()` reported a synthetic `http.disconnect`, which made `with_cancellation` cancel every filtered request (empty response) and would have truncated streaming responses.

## Validation

Unit tests (`tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_unicode_filter_middleware.py`, 18 cases) run the middleware against a FastAPI echo app and include a regression test that uses the real `with_cancellation` decorator and a `StreamingResponse` test; both fail on the previous revision and pass now.

End-to-end tests (`tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_unicode_filter_integration.py`) start `vllm serve hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM --load-format dummy` with the flag set and check, via `usage.prompt_tokens`/`input_tokens` against the unfiltered `/tokenize` endpoint, that chat, completions (`echo=True`), streaming chat, Responses and Anthropic Messages requests all drop the tag characters. Both test files live under `tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/`, which the Entrypoints Integration CI step collects.

```
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_unicode_filter_middleware.py -v
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/serve/middleware/test_unicode_filter_integration.py -v
pre-commit run --files $(git diff --name-only upstream/main HEAD)
```

Results on an RTX 3500 Ada (12 GB), vLLM at the PR commit:

| Suite | Fixed middleware | Pre-fix middleware (same tests) |
|---|---|---|
| Unit (`test_unicode_filter_middleware.py`) | 18 passed | 6 failed (cancellation, streaming, escapes, pattern) |
| Real server (`test_unicode_filter_integration.py`) | 7 passed | 6 of 7 failed (empty bodies, no stream events, unfiltered token counts on Responses/Anthropic); control passed |
| `pre-commit run --files ...` | all hooks pass | n/a |

Server used by the integration test: `vllm serve hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM --load-format dummy --max-model-len 512 --enforce-eager --max-num-seqs 2 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.3` with `VLLM_ENABLE_UNICODE_FILTERING_MIDDLEWARE=true`.

## Details

- Pure ASGI middleware (`vllm/entrypoints/serve/middleware/unicode_filter.py`), registered in `init_entrypoints_middleware` inside the authentication middleware so unauthenticated requests are rejected before any body is buffered.
- Filtering runs on the UTF-8 bytes: every codepoint in the block is a 4-byte sequence with prefix `F3 A0 80|81`, so one bytes regex covers the block without a decode/encode round trip. A second regex handles the JSON surrogate-pair escape and leaves escaped backslashes (`\\uDB40`) alone, since those are literal text.
- The body is buffered once in the middleware and replayed to the app; after the replay, `receive()` defers to the server's own `receive()` so disconnect detection keeps working.
- Limitation: only JSON-encoded tag characters in the request body are handled; characters that arrive through other channels (for example, a prompt fetched by the model from a tool result) are out of scope.
- The toggle is an environment variable, matching the predecessor PR's approved design; a `FrontendArgs` flag would also fit if maintainers prefer that.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for the rebase, the bug fix, the tests and this description; every line was reviewed by the submitter, and the commands above were run locally on an RTX 3500 Ada (12 GB).

+## Unicode Tag-Block Filtering
+
+The following environment variable controls sanitization of incoming request payloads. It is intended to clean up requests from clients that emit unwanted Unicode content — specifically, Unicode tag characters (`U+E0020`-`U+E007F`), which are invisible to humans but are tokenized by language models and can cause unpredictable responses. When enabled, these characters are stripped from the bodies of `POST` requests to the LLM generation endpoints: `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/chat/completions/batch`, `/v1/completions`, `/v1/responses`, `/v1/messages` and `/cohere/v2/chat`. All other endpoints, methods, and Unicode characters (including emojis) are unaffected.
+
+To enable it, set the following environment variable before starting the server:
+
+```bash
+VLLM_ENABLE_UNICODE_FILTERING_MIDDLEWARE=true vllm serve ...
+```
+
+Filtering operates directly on the UTF-8 bytes of the request body and handles both ways a JSON client can encode these characters: the raw UTF-8 sequence, and the JSON `\u` escape of the equivalent surrogate pair (`\uDB40\uDC20`-`\uDB40\uDC7F`, which is what Python's `json.dumps` emits by default). Clean payloads are detected with a quick substring check and skip the regex entirely. The flag defaults to off, so existing deployments are unaffected unless explicitly enabled.
+
 ## API Reference
 
 ### Completions API

@@ -0,0 +1,182 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""End-to-end tests for ``UnicodeFilterMiddleware`` against a real
+``vllm serve`` process.
+
+The unit tests cover the byte filtering in isolation; these tests check the
+middleware inside the real API server stack, where the generation handlers
+are wrapped in ``with_cancellation`` and stream through ``StreamingResponse``.
+Dummy weights keep startup fast: the assertions only depend on tokenization,
+not on model output.
+"""
+
+import json
+from collections.abc import Callable
+
+import httpx
+import pytest
+
+from tests.utils import RemoteOpenAIServer
+
+MODEL_NAME = "hmellor/tiny-random-LlamaForCausalLM"
+# Characters from the Unicode "Tags" block (U+E0020 - U+E007F).
+TAG_CHARS = "".join(chr(c) for c in (0xE0020, 0xE0024, 0xE0041, 0xE007F))
+CLEAN_PROMPT = "Tell me a story about a dragon"
+TAGGED_PROMPT = f"Tell me a {TAG_CHARS}story about a dragon"
+
+# Encoders for the two ways a JSON client can send tag characters.
+ENCODERS: dict[str, Callable[[dict], bytes]] = {
+    "raw-utf8": lambda payload: json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False).encode(),
+    "json-escaped": lambda payload: json.dumps(payload).encode(),
+}
+
+
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def server():
+    args = [
+        "--load-format",
+        "dummy",
+        "--max-model-len",
+        "512",
+        "--enforce-eager",
+        "--max-num-seqs",
+        "2",
+        "--gpu-memory-utilization",
+        "0.3",
+    ]
+    env_dict = {"VLLM_ENABLE_UNICODE_FILTERING_MIDDLEWARE": "true"}
+    with RemoteOpenAIServer(MODEL_NAME, args, env_dict=env_dict) as remote_server:
+        yield remote_server
+
+
+def _post(server: RemoteOpenAIServer, path: str, body: bytes) -> httpx.Response:
+    return httpx.post(
+        server.url_for(path),
+        content=body,
+        headers={"content-type": "application/json"},
+        timeout=60.0,
+    )
+
+
+def _token_count(server: RemoteOpenAIServer, prompt: str) -> int:
+    """Count prompt tokens through ``/tokenize``, which is not filtered."""
+    response = _post(
+        server, "tokenize", json.dumps({"model": MODEL_NAME, "prompt": prompt})
+    )
+    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+    return response.json()["count"]
+
+
+def test_tag_characters_are_tokenized_when_not_filtered(server: RemoteOpenAIServer):
+    """Control: without filtering, the tag characters cost extra tokens, so a
+    matching token count on filtered routes proves they were stripped."""
+    assert _token_count(server, TAGGED_PROMPT) > _token_count(server, CLEAN_PROMPT)
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("encoding", ENCODERS)
+def test_chat_completion_strips_tag_characters(
+    server: RemoteOpenAIServer, encoding: str
+):
+    encode = ENCODERS[encoding]
+
+    def chat(content: str) -> dict:
+        response = _post(
+            server,
+            "v1/chat/completions",
+            encode(
+                {
+                    "model": MODEL_NAME,
+                    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": content}],
+                    "max_tokens": 1,
+                }
+            ),
+        )
+        assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+        return response.json()
+
+    clean, tagged = chat(CLEAN_PROMPT), chat(TAGGED_PROMPT)
+    assert tagged["choices"] and tagged["choices"][0]["message"] is not None
+    assert tagged["usage"]["prompt_tokens"] == clean["usage"]["prompt_tokens"]
+
+
+def test_completion_echo_returns_stripped_prompt(server: RemoteOpenAIServer):
+    response = _post(
+        server,
+        "v1/completions",
+        ENCODERS["raw-utf8"](
+            {
+                "model": MODEL_NAME,
+                "prompt": TAGGED_PROMPT,
+                "max_tokens": 1,
+                "echo": True,
+            }
+        ),
+    )
+    assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+    body = response.json()
+    echoed = body["choices"][0]["text"]
+    assert not any(ch in echoed for ch in TAG_CHARS), repr(echoed)
+    assert body["usage"]["prompt_tokens"] == _token_count(server, CLEAN_PROMPT)
+
+
+def test_streaming_chat_completion_runs_to_completion(server: RemoteOpenAIServer):
+    """The replayed request body must not look like a client disconnect, or
+    the stream is cancelled before the first chunk."""
+    body = ENCODERS["raw-utf8"](
+        {
+            "model": MODEL_NAME,
+            "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": TAGGED_PROMPT}],
+            "max_tokens": 3,
+            "stream": True,
+        }
+    )
+    events = []
+    with httpx.stream(
+        "POST",
+        server.url_for("v1/chat/completions"),
+        content=body,
+        headers={"content-type": "application/json"},
+        timeout=60.0,
+    ) as response:
+        assert response.status_code == 200
+        for line in response.iter_lines():
+            if line.startswith("data: "):
+                events.append(line.removeprefix("data: "))
+
+    assert events and events[-1] == "[DONE]"
+    assert all("choices" in json.loads(event) for event in events[:-1])
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    ("path", "build_payload", "usage_key"),
+    [
+        (
+            "v1/responses",
+            lambda text: {"model": MODEL_NAME, "input": text, "max_output_tokens": 1},
+            "input_tokens",
+        ),
+        (
+            "v1/messages",
+            lambda text: {
+                "model": MODEL_NAME,
+                "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": text}],
+                "max_tokens": 1,
+            },
+            "input_tokens",
+        ),
+    ],
+    ids=["responses", "anthropic-messages"],
+)
+def test_other_generation_apis_strip_tag_characters(
+    server: RemoteOpenAIServer,
+    path: str,
+    build_payload: Callable[[str], dict],
+    usage_key: str,
+):
+    def usage(text: str) -> int:
+        response = _post(server, path, ENCODERS["raw-utf8"](build_payload(text)))
+        assert response.status_code == 200, response.text
+        return response.json()["usage"][usage_key]
+
+    assert usage(TAGGED_PROMPT) == usage(CLEAN_PROMPT)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+"""Unit tests for ``UnicodeFilterMiddleware``.
+
+These tests exercise the middleware in isolation against a tiny FastAPI echo
+app, so they do not require a vLLM engine.
+"""
+
+import asyncio
+import json
+
+import httpx
+import pytest
+from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
+from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse
+from pydantic import BaseModel
+
+from vllm.entrypoints.serve.middleware.unicode_filter import (
+    UnicodeFilterMiddleware,
+)
+from vllm.entrypoints.serve.utils.api_utils import with_cancellation
+
+# A few characters from the Unicode "Tags" block (U+E0020 - U+E007F)
+# that the middleware is supposed to strip.
+TAG_CHARS = "".join(chr(c) for c in (0xE0020, 0xE0024, 0xE0041, 0xE007F))
+# The same characters as JSON "\\u" escapes, which is how json.dumps emits
+# them by default (ensure_ascii=True).
+TAG_CHARS_ESCAPED = json.dumps(TAG_CHARS)[1:-1]
+ROUTES = sorted(UnicodeFilterMiddleware.ROUTES_TO_FILTER)
+
+
+def _build_app() -> FastAPI:
+    """A FastAPI app whose routes echo the bytes they received."""
+    app = FastAPI()
+
+    async def echo(request: Request) -> dict:
+        body = await request.body()
+        return {"body": body.decode("utf-8")}
+
+    for route in ROUTES:
+        app.post(route)(echo)
+    app.post("/health")(echo)
+
+    @app.get("/v1/chat/completions")
+    async def chat_completions_get() -> dict:
+        return {"ok": True}
+
+    app.add_middleware(UnicodeFilterMiddleware)
+    return app
+
+
+async def _post(app: FastAPI, path: str, payload: str) -> httpx.Response:
+    transport = httpx.ASGITransport(app=app)
+    async with httpx.AsyncClient(
+        transport=transport, base_url="http://testserver"
+    ) as client:
+        return await client.post(
+            path,
+            content=payload.encode("utf-8"),
+            headers={"content-type": "application/json"},
+        )
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("path", ROUTES)
+async def test_strips_tag_block_characters(path: str) -> None:
+    app = _build_app()
+    payload = f"Hello{TAG_CHARS}World"
+
+    response = await _post(app, path, payload)
+
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert response.json()["body"] == "HelloWorld"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "escaped",
+    [TAG_CHARS_ESCAPED, TAG_CHARS_ESCAPED.upper().replace("\\U", "\\u")],
+    ids=["lowercase-hex", "uppercase-hex"],
+)
+async def test_strips_json_escaped_tag_characters(escaped: str) -> None:
+    app = _build_app()
+    payload = f'{{"prompt": "Hello{escaped}World"}}'
+
+    response = await _post(app, "/v1/completions", payload)
+
+    assert response.status_code == 200
+    assert json.loads(response.json()["body"]) == {"prompt": "HelloWorld"}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_mixed_raw_and_escaped_tag_characters_are_stripped() -> None:
+    app = _build_app()
+    payload = f'{{"prompt": "a{TAG_CHARS}b{TAG_CHARS_ESCAPED}c"}}'
+
+    response = await _post(app, "/v1/completions", payload)
+
+    assert json.loads(response.json()["body"]) == {"prompt": "abc"}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.asyncio
+async def test_escaped_backslash_is_not_treated_as_an_escape() -> None:
+    """``\\\\udb40\\\\udc41`` in JSON text is a literal backslash followed by
+    plain text, not a tag character, and must be left untouched."""
+    app = _build_app()
+    payload = '{"prompt": "a\\\\udb40\\\\udc41b"}'
+

+        assert escaped.search(json.dumps(chr(cp)).encode()) is None, hex(cp)

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+from typing import ClassVar
+
+import regex as re
+from starlette.types import ASGIApp, Message, Receive, Scope, Send
+
+from vllm.logger import init_logger
+
+logger = init_logger(__name__)
+
+
+class UnicodeFilterMiddleware:
+    """Pure ASGI middleware that strips Unicode tag characters (U+E0020 to
+    U+E007F) from request bodies sent to LLM generation endpoints.
+
+    These characters are invisible to humans but are tokenized by language
+    models, which can lead to unpredictable responses. The middleware is
+    intended to clean up requests from clients that emit unwanted Unicode
+    content. Normal Unicode, including emojis, is left untouched. Only POST
+    requests whose path matches :attr:`ROUTES_TO_FILTER` are inspected; all
+    other traffic passes through unchanged.
+
+    Filtering is performed directly on the UTF-8 bytes of the body, so no
+    decode/encode round trip is needed, and both encodings a JSON client can
+    use for these characters are handled: the raw UTF-8 sequence (``F3 A0 80
+    A0`` to ``F3 A0 81 BF``) and the JSON ``\\u`` escape of the equivalent
+    surrogate pair (``\\uDB40\\uDC20`` to ``\\uDB40\\uDC7F``). The common
+    (clean) case is ruled out with cheap substring checks that skip the
+    regexes entirely.
+    """
+
+    ROUTES_TO_FILTER: ClassVar[frozenset[str]] = frozenset(
+        {
+            "/v1/chat/completions",
+            "/v1/chat/completions/batch",
+            "/v1/completions",
+            "/v1/responses",
+            "/v1/messages",
+            "/cohere/v2/chat",
+        }
+    )
+
+    # UTF-8 encodings of U+E0020..U+E007F:
+    #   U+E0020..U+E003F -> F3 A0 80 [A0-BF]
+    #   U+E0040..U+E007F -> F3 A0 81 [80-BF]
+    TAGS_BLOCK_PATTERN: ClassVar[re.Pattern[bytes]] = re.compile(
+        b"\xf3\xa0(?:\x80[\xa0-\xbf]|\x81[\x80-\xbf])"
+    )
+    # JSON-escaped UTF-16 surrogate pairs for the same range, in either hex
+    # case. Only an odd run of backslashes starts an escape (``\\uDB40`` is a
+    # literal backslash followed by text), so group 1 captures and keeps any
+    # preceding escaped backslashes.
+    TAGS_BLOCK_ESCAPED_PATTERN: ClassVar[re.Pattern[bytes]] = re.compile(
+        rb"(?<!\\)((?:\\\\)*)\\u[dD][bB]40\\u[dD][cC][2-7][0-9a-fA-F]"
+    )
+
+    def __init__(self, app: ASGIApp) -> None:
+        self.app = app
+
+    @classmethod
+    def strip_tag_characters(cls, body: bytes) -> bytes:
+        if b"\xf3\xa0\x80" in body or b"\xf3\xa0\x81" in body:
+            body = cls.TAGS_BLOCK_PATTERN.sub(b"", body)
+        if b"\\u" in body:
+            body = cls.TAGS_BLOCK_ESCAPED_PATTERN.sub(rb"\1", body)
+        return body
+
+    async def __call__(self, scope: Scope, receive: Receive, send: Send) -> None:
+        if scope["type"] != "http" or scope.get("method") != "POST":
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+
+        root_path = scope.get("root_path", "")
+        path = scope["path"].removeprefix(root_path)
+        if path not in self.ROUTES_TO_FILTER:
+            await self.app(scope, receive, send)
+            return
+
+        # Buffer the whole body so it can be rewritten before the downstream
+        # handlers see it.
+        body = bytearray()
+        more_body = True
+        while more_body:
+            message = await receive()
+            if message["type"] == "http.disconnect":
+
+                async def disconnect_receive() -> Message:
+                    return {"type": "http.disconnect"}
+
+                await self.app(scope, disconnect_receive, send)
+                return
+            body.extend(message.get("body", b""))
+            more_body = message.get("more_body", False)
+
+        body_bytes = self.strip_tag_characters(bytes(body))
+        if len(body_bytes) != len(body):
+            logger.debug(
+                "UnicodeFilterMiddleware stripped tag characters from %s", path
+            )
+
+        # Keep Content-Length consistent with the (possibly rewritten) body.
+        new_headers = [
+            (k, v)
+            for k, v in scope.get("headers", [])
+            if k.lower() != b"content-length"
+        ]
+        new_headers.append((b"content-length", str(len(body_bytes)).encode()))
+        scope = {**scope, "headers": new_headers}
+
+        body_sent = False
+
+        async def replay_receive() -> Message:
+            nonlocal body_sent
+            if not body_sent:
+                body_sent = True
+                return {
+                    "type": "http.request",
+                    "body": body_bytes,
+                    "more_body": False,
+                }
+            # The body has been handed over; defer to the server's receive()
+            # so later calls block until the client really disconnects, as
+            # ``with_cancellation`` and ``StreamingResponse`` expect.
+            return await receive()
+
+        await self.app(scope, replay_receive, send)
